summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:
- **ASFA (42 U.S.C. §§ 671–675)** — court ‘reasonable efforts’ findings; permanency timelines  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

primary_citations.citation_text: Texas - Texas Family Code Chapter 261 (Investigation of Report of Child Abuse or Neglect)
Texas - Texas Family Code Chapter 262 (Procedures in Suit by Governmental Entity to Protect Health and Safety of Child)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Texas Department of Family & Protective Services
key_cases.holding: The mass removal of children from the YFZ Ranch was not warranted on the evidence, because Chapter 262 requires danger to the individual child and the Family Code gives courts ample authority to protect children without separating them from their parents.
key_cases.relevance: The Texas Supreme Court's controlling application of Family Code §§ 262.101-.201 at this node: danger must be proved as to the particular child, and the court must use the Code's lesser alternatives — orders restraining a party, removing the alleged perpetrator, or assisting the investigation — before separating a family.
key_cases.quote: the Family Code gives the district court broad authority to protect children short of separating them from their parents and placing them in foster care

key_cases.case_name: Roe v. Texas Department of Protective & Regulatory Services
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
key_cases.holding: A CPS caseworker's visual body-cavity search of a child raised a Fourth Amendment claim, and in non-exigent circumstances the worker must obtain a warrant or court order rather than proceed on a parent's silence; a parent's consent to an investigative home interview is not consent to such a search, and consent to entry may be revoked. Because those rights were not clearly established, the worker received qualified immunity.
key_cases.relevance: Identifies the Family Code route by which a court orders an examination or entry the parent has refused — the court-ordered assistance mechanism that this node turns on.
key_cases.quote: In non-exigent circumstances, the worker then has time to obtain a warrant either personally to conduct a visual body cavity search or to have a physician perform it.

search_keywords: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services

state_agency.name: Texas Department of Family and Protective Services

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — Tex. Fam. Code § 261.101(a)

Professionals must report not later than the 24th hour — Tex. Fam. Code § 261.101(b) (teachers, nurses, doctors, day-care employees, juvenile probation officers, juvenile detention or correctional officers, and others licensed or certified by the state who have direct contact with children)

The duty applies without exception to otherwise privileged communications, including attorneys, clergy, medical practitioners, social workers and mental health professionals — Tex. Fam. Code § 261.101(c)
reporting_details: In Texas any person with reasonable cause to believe a child has been abused or neglected must report it immediately, and a professional must report not later than the 24th hour after first having that belief (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.101(a)-(b)).

other: Forcing or coercing a child to enter into a marriage

common_failures: Accepting a hotline report from a caller who will not give a name and telephone number — the department is not authorized to accept an anonymous report and must refer the caller to law enforcement (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.104(b))

notice_requirements.timing: On first contact with the parent or with the alleged perpetrator after the department initiates an investigation of a parent or other person having legal custody of a child; before taking any action under Tex. Fam. Code § 261.304 the department representative must provide the representative's identity, the written summary, and a reasonable amount of time to read or review the summary (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a), (b-1))
content_required: The department's procedures for conducting an investigation, including when it would request to remove the child through the judicial system, that the law requires every report to be referred to a law enforcement agency for a separate determination of whether a criminal violation occurred, and that any statement or admission made to anyone may be used against the person in a criminal case, as a basis to remove a child, or as a basis to terminate the person's relationship with a child (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(1)(C)(i))

The person's right to file a complaint with the department or request a review of the findings, the right to review all records of the investigation unless review would jeopardize an ongoing criminal investigation or the child's safety, and the right to seek legal counsel (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(1)(C)(ii)-(iv))

References to the statutory and regulatory provisions governing child abuse and neglect and how to obtain copies, the process to acquire access to the child if the child is removed, and the known allegations the department is investigating (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(1)(C)(v)-(vi), (viii))

Verbal notification of the rights to refuse to speak with any agent of the department without legal counsel present; to receive assistance from an attorney and to a court-appointed attorney if the person is indigent, is the parent, and the department seeks a court order under § 262.101, § 262.105, or § 264.203; to record any interaction or interview, subject to disclosure under a court order; to refuse to allow the investigator to enter the home or interview the child without a court order; to have legal counsel present before allowing entry or an interview; to withhold consent to release of medical or mental health records and to any medical or psychological examination of the child; to refuse a drug test; and to consult legal counsel before agreeing to any proposed voluntary safety plan (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(2))

If the department determines removal may be warranted, a proposed child placement resources form instructing the parent to identify at least three individuals who could be relative or designated caregivers, to ask the child to identify a potential caregiver, and stating a location available 24 hours a day to submit the form (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(3))
The informational manual required by Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3071 (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(4))
notice_requirements.language_requirements: The written summary must be brief and easily understood and written in a language that the person understands, or, if the person is illiterate, read to the person in a language that the person understands (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(a)(1)(A)-(B)). The informational manuals required by § 261.3071 must be provided in both English and Spanish (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3071(c))
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: If a person who is the subject of an investigation does not receive the verbal notification and written summary required by this section, any information obtained from the person, and any other information that would not have been discovered without that information, is not admissible for use against the person in any civil proceeding (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(e)). The investigator must document that the verbal notification was given, and the department must provide a true and correct copy of the signed verification form to the person or the person's attorney (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.307(c)-(d))

notice_requirements.timing: Orally and in writing before the department conducts an interview with an alleged perpetrator (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027(a))
content_required: That the person may create an audio or video recording of the interview but may not record the interview in any other manner (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027(a)(1))
That any audio or video recording made by the person may be subject to subpoena under a court order (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027(a)(2))
That the person may request and receive a copy of the department's current recording policy (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027(a)(3))
notice_requirements.defective_notice_consequence: Not specified in Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027. The department must document in the case file that it provided the notice and must provide two copies of the written notice to be signed by the person, giving one signed notice to the person and retaining the other in the case file (Tex. Fam. Code § 261.3027(b)-(c))
